task: Predict totalItemsSold for a (sneakerName, buyerRegion) pair for a GENUINELY NEW product -- true cold start, not a restock of an existing SKU.

training_data.grouping: one row per (sneakerName, buyerRegion) -- full 50x51 grid, includes zero-transaction combos with totalItemsSold = 0
training_data.split_strategy: GroupShuffleSplit on sneakerName, test_size=0.2, random_state=42 -- every region for a given sneaker stays entirely in train or entirely in test, so this tests generalization to a genuinely UNSEEN sneaker

tuning.method: GridSearchCV with GroupKFold(5) respecting sneaker groups, scoring=neg_mean_absolute_error

notes: Best-performing model of the five tried in modeling_new_product.ipynb (XGBoost-Poisson, XGBoost-Tweedie, CatBoost-Poisson, CatBoost-Tweedie, HistGradientBoosting-Poisson) on the genuine cold-start task.

sneakerName is deliberately excluded from features -- it won't exist for a real new product -- so generalization relies on brand/retailPrice/silhouette/colorwayType/historicalBrandRegionDemand instead.

Test metrics here are notably weaker than the existing-product models (hist_gradient_boosting_regressor_poisson, xgb__regressor_tweedie) because this is a genuinely harder task -- unseen sneakers, not just unseen (sneaker, region) combos of known sneakers.
